title: Don't Just Teach Skills — Expose Confidently Held Misconceptions
tagline: The reef doesn't care what you believe. It only cares what you do.
summary: Most entrepreneurs don't fail because they lack skill — they fail because they act on beliefs they've never tested. This introductory module starts with the learner, not the content: surfacing self-limiting beliefs, separating fact from prediction, and building the habit of experimenting despite disbelief. It establishes the experiential, evidence-driven posture every later module depends on.

learningObjectives.statement: Identify a self-limiting belief about one's own abilities and reclassify it as an untested prediction rather than a settled fact.
Design a small, low-stakes experiment that produces real evidence about a belief, attempting it with AI assistance even when confidence is absent.
Diagnose a failed attempt as an ability gap, a persistence gap, or an approach gap, and interpret the evidence accordingly.
Develop a personal rubric for judging the quality of one's own work rather than depending on external grading.
Distinguish goals one has genuinely chosen from goals inherited from others' expectations, and articulate at least one authentic motivation.
Examine one's own 'why' against a human-values standard — building to improve the world, not merely to extract value — and judge whether it can sustain sustained effort.

lessons.title: Prediction vs. Fact — The Self-Limiting Belief Audit

activities.title: Run the five-question Self-Limiting Belief Audit on one belief
State one belief as a prediction and list the evidence you actually have
The Experiment Protocol; the three reasons something doesn't work
Attempt one small task with AI assistance and log expected vs. actual
Diagnose a past failure as ability, persistence, or approach
Building your own rubric; chosen vs. inherited goals; human values in an AI economy
Draft a personal 'how do I know if this is good?' rubric
Separate what you want from what you think you should want

assessments.method: Reflective coaching conversation (simulation 'The First Attempt') in which the learner surfaces an untested belief, designs a 24-hour experiment, and names an authentic want
assessments.successCriteria: Names a specific belief as a prediction, proposes a concrete 24-hour experiment, and articulates at least one genuinely chosen want (debrief score of 6 or higher).

assessments.method: Written experiment log: one attempt made with AI assistance, the expected-vs-actual result, a failure diagnosis, and a self-applied quality rubric
assessments.successCriteria: Logs a real attempt, classifies the outcome as ability/persistence/approach with justification, and judges the work against a self-authored rubric.
